title: Walden; or, Life in the Woods

access.edition_or_version: First published 9 August 1854, Ticknor and Fields, Boston (imprint verified 2026-09-24); public-domain text.

tone_mechanisms_observed: aphoristic declaratives and interrogatives addressed to an implied reader, arising from concrete measured detail
alternation of exact observational catalogues (dimensions, dates, costs) with expansive reflective periods — concreteness licenses generalization
narrated past of the two-year sojourn punctuated by timeless-present aphorism
life-as-experiment self-monitoring frame: the narrator tests his own life at a slight distance
mechanics.point_of_view: First person, didactic and self-experimenting; reflection tied to seasonal and diary time so meditation never floats free.
mechanics.tense_and_structure: Past narration of the sojourn against gnomic present-tense axioms; the movement between the two is the reflective rhythm, and periodization (chapters paced as walks) keeps it anchored.
mechanics.rhythm_and_cadence: Slow, accretive cadence with the aphorism as resting point; chapters pace as walks.
mechanics.psychic_distance: Close on experience but explicitly self-monitoring — the tested-life frame is self-distancing (see clm-tone-reflective-self-distanced-reflection).
mechanics.style_and_devices: Analogy between outer labor and inner economy; metaphor of measurement (ruling, counting) applied to the examined life; figure grown from observed detail — a pond, an ant, a thaw.
mechanics.copyright_note: Public domain. Described by technique only; no passage reproduced.
